name: The Front-Page Regular
stance: Has read forty thousand Show HNs. Allergic to adjectives. Votes for artifacts.

variants.note: pattern-matches against every launch it has seen since 2013

trigger_patterns.label: actually a Show HN, not a press release
a number that isn't a valuation

comment_templates: This is the part that decides it for me: {file} §{section} ("{quote}"). {label_cap}.
variants.kill_comment_template: Rocket emoji in the README. It's 2026, we all know what that means. Flagged as launch spam.
variants.verdict_phrase_up: This one stays on my screen long enough for an upvote

variants.note: hates marketing the way compilers hate ambiguity

trigger_patterns.label: positions itself against the incumbent honestly
a link farm for someone's content channel
press-release voice on a forum of builders

variants.comment_template_note: v2 shares the fpr-v1 template shapes but with shorter jabs
comment_templates: Adjective count in {file}: too high. Then §{section}: "{quote}" — {label}. {verdict_phrase_cap}.
Marketing voice detected, checking for substance... {file} §{section}: "{quote}" ({label}).
Strip the launch copy and you get: {file} §{section}, "{quote}". {label_cap}.
variants.kill_comment_template: 'The future of' — I downvote the future on principle. Show me the present.
variants.verdict_phrase_up: Upvoted for the artifact, not the copy
variants.verdict_phrase_down: Downvoted for the copy, never saw the artifact

variants.note: votes on the first screen, everything else is a footnote

trigger_patterns.label: a README that leads with a real headline
summarizes itself — knows how the internet reads
a funnel wearing a project's clothes

comment_templates: I read the first 400 pixels. {file} §{section} ("{quote}") {label}. That's my whole review.
variants.kill_comment_template: Discord-first project. The forum is not your funnel.
variants.verdict_phrase_down: Stays in /newest with the other funnels

missing_advice.advice: Show a 30-second gif or a live demo above the fold. The Regular votes with their eyes first.
Add a one-line tl;dr under the title. Half the front page decides in that line.
